approach: Rebuild the verified candidate on the tip: producer cargo commands take a build slot through an `athena` symlink named `cargo`. (1) policy.rs: `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` becomes pub and a new `cargo_subcommand(args)` uses it; `check_cargo` is untouched. (2) env.rs: `CargoShim` and `install_cargo_shim` (producer only) create `<job_dir>/agent/bin/cargo -> athena`, put that dir first on PATH and set the `ATHENA_SLOT_*` variables. The wrapper's wait is `producer_slot_wait_s(build_wait_s, bash_default_timeout_ms)` = min(build_wait_s, Bash default timeout minus 60 s, at least 1 s). So with the defaults (1800 s and 600 s) it is 540 s, and the wrapper times out, writes its note and exits 75 before the agent's Bash tool kills it (finding 1). `env::build` is unchanged. (3) athena-cli/src/slot_exec.rs is the wrapper; main.rs dispatches on argv[0]=cargo before clap. It gates build/test/clippy/check through `SlotQueue::acquire(Class::Producer)`. On `SlotWait` it writes the wait note, prints 'no build slot free for N s; try again' and exits 75. The nested-cargo guard `ATHENA_SLOT_HELD` carries the slot dir path and counts only when it equals the wrapper's own `ATHENA_SLOT_DIR`. A test binary that runs under a producer's wrapper therefore cannot switch off the slot in a test's own temp queue (finding 2). (4) slots.rs gets wait-note helpers. (5) `producer_loop` installs the shim on `spec.env`, clears the note before each invocation and reads it after. A note becomes a `SlotWait` error, which `produce_and_verify` turns into `hold_for_slot_wait`. The hold wording in close.rs and the `go` message in mod.rs are widened to cover a producer-stage hold with no candidate (finding 4). (6) Tests, the shard-timings line, CHANGELOG and the design doc.

decisions.choice: The wrapper is the `athena` binary reached through a symlink named `cargo`; main.rs checks the argv[0] basename before parsing arguments, as it already does for the hook names (main.rs:572-580).
decisions.reason: No new binary and no unsafe code; `SlotQueue` is reused unchanged. The policy already denies a program name containing `/`, so the agent's `cargo` resolves to the shim.

rejected.why: A shell script is a non-Rust file and adds a quoting layer.

rejected.option: Slot gating inside the pre-tool-use hook
rejected.why: A hook runs before the command and cannot hold a slot for its whole run.

decisions.choice: The subcommand is found by a new `policy::cargo_subcommand`, which uses the one public `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS`. `check_cargo` keeps its own loop and messages; an agreement test ties the two.
decisions.reason: Root cause: a lookup that reads only args[0] lets `cargo -q build` skip the queue. One shared list means every flag the policy accepts is also skipped by the wrapper (criterion 7).

rejected.option: A copy of the flag list in the wrapper
rejected.why: It would drift from the policy; criterion 7 forbids a second copy.

rejected.option: Rewrite `check_cargo` on top of the helper
rejected.why: It has per-case messages; the refactor adds risk for no gain.

decisions.choice: An option before the subcommand that is not in the list (--config, -Z, +nightly) makes the wrapper run the real cargo with no slot.
decisions.reason: The policy hook denies those forms before the command runs, so an agent never reaches the wrapper with them. Gating `cargo --version` would only slow cheap calls. A unit test records the choice.

rejected.option: Fail closed: take a slot on any unknown leading option
rejected.why: It gates harmless commands, and the policy already makes the case unreachable.

decisions.choice: The wrapper sets `ATHENA_SLOT_HELD=<slot dir path>` on the real cargo. A wrapper honours it only when it equals its own `ATHENA_SLOT_DIR`, and then runs the real cargo with no slot.
decisions.reason: A cargo test that itself runs `cargo` resolves to the shim again; with one slot it would deadlock against its parent. Tying the value to the slot dir answers finding 2: this repository's slot_exec tests, run by a later producer's `cargo test` through the shim, inherit the producer's HELD value, but their temp slot dir differs, so the guard does not fire and the tests still see the slot held. The tests also start every child with env_clear. The policy refuses env assignments in agent commands (policy.rs:546-553), so an agent cannot set it.

rejected.why: Inherited by any test that runs under a producer's wrapper, which turns off its slot (finding 2).

rejected.option: Remove the shim from the child's PATH
rejected.why: It changes what build scripts and tests see, and a child can be handed a path with the shim in it.

decisions.choice: The wrapper's wait is `env::producer_slot_wait_s(build_wait_s, bash_default_timeout_ms)` = min(build_wait_s, (bash_default_timeout_ms/1000).saturating_sub(60)), floored at 1 s. `install_cargo_shim` computes it from `CargoShim.build_wait_s` and `CargoShim.bash_default_timeout_ms` (from `jc.config.pipeline()` and `spec.agents`) and sets `ATHENA_SLOT_WAIT_S`; `SlotWait.limit_s` is this value.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: athena.toml:64-65 sets Bash timeouts of 600 s default and 1200 s max, and config.rs:166 defaults build_wait_s to 1800. A wait of 1800 s would be killed by the Bash tool first, so the exit-75, note and hold path would be unreachable. The default timeout (the lower of the two) is used because the agent can pass any timeout up to the max but gets the default when it passes none. The 60 s margin lets the wrapper write the note and print its message; it is not a promise about build time. With the shipped settings the cap is 540 s, and the design doc says so in place of 1800 s.

rejected.option: Keep build_wait_s (1800 s) and say the hold is unreachable by default
rejected.why: It would ship a path that never runs in real use.
It splits the rule into two places and cannot be unit-tested without a full wrapper run; install_cargo_shim already has both numbers.
An agent that passes no timeout is killed at 600 s.

decisions.choice: On timeout the wrapper exits 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) with 'no build slot free for <limit> s; try again' and writes a `SlotWait` JSON note at `ATHENA_SLOT_NOTE`. After each producer invocation the run reads the note and holds the job through `hold_for_slot_wait`. A later command does not clear the note (finding 2 of the old job, kept); it is cleared only before the next invocation.
decisions.reason: Exit 75 matches agent-and-build-slots.md:164 and is an environment code, not a policy denial. The note carries the wait to the run, which reuses the hold path that disk.rs, drain.rs:4325 and `go` (mod.rs:479-489) already read.

rejected.option: Count exit 75 as a failed producer
rejected.why: It uses an attempt for an environment condition; the brief requires held, not failed.

rejected.option: Hold from the wrapper's own process
rejected.why: It has no job records or state directory.

decisions.choice: Gate only build, test, clippy and check. run, doc, fmt, metadata and tree take no slot.
decisions.reason: The brief names the four and puts a change to the allowed commands out of scope.

rejected.why: Beyond the brief; recorded as a risk.

decisions.choice: Tests drive the shipped binary through the shim made by `install_cargo_shim`, against a `/bin/sh` fake cargo later on PATH. Each child is started with env_clear plus only the env that install_cargo_shim returns (with an explicit PATH). A `SlotQueue` over the same dir observes the slot from outside.
decisions.reason: It exercises the argv[0] dispatch, PATH order, real-cargo lookup, flag walk and slot hold together, and does not depend on the environment of whoever runs the tests. The fake records arguments and blocks on a file; all slot logic is production code.

rejected.why: It would miss the main.rs dispatch and the PATH install.

decisions.choice: The stop closure passed to `acquire` stays `|| Ok(())`. The open question on process groups is dropped: crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs:4 says the driver spawns `claude -p` in a new process group, and claude.rs:394 calls `kill_group(pgid, GRACE)` on a deadline, stall or the kill switch, so a waiting wrapper in that group is stopped with its agent.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: the code answers it, and the wrapper has no Registry access to poll the kill switch itself.

rejected.option: Poll the kill switch in the wrapper
rejected.why: The wrapper process has no Registry or state dir; the group kill already covers it.

decisions.choice: Widen the hold wording for the producer stage: the `hold_for_slot_wait` doc in close.rs:191-197 gets hold_for_disk's no-candidate phrasing, and the `go` message at mod.rs:485 says 'from its kept candidate if it has one, from the start if not'.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: a producer-stage hold has no candidate and no resume mark, as hold_for_disk's doc (close.rs:170-172) already says for the before-producer case. disk.rs:297 already reads 'a drain resumes it when a build slot is free', so the marker text needs no change. No test asserts the mod.rs:485 text (searched).

rejected.why: It would tell the user a candidate exists when none does.

decisions.choice: The earlier candidate's other choices stay: SIGKILL of the wrapper frees the slot while the child may still run (workspace denies unsafe, so no exec); stale-target-dir finding needs no code; this retry answers the stale-branch finding by rebuilding on the tip.
decisions.reason: The brief says to keep these.

risks.risk: A child cargo that resolves `cargo` through PATH queues behind its own parent and deadlocks.
risks.mitigation: ATHENA_SLOT_HELD (slot dir path) guard, and a test where the fake cargo calls the shim again with one slot, which must complete.

risks.risk: The wait cap (default 540 s) is shorter than build_wait_s, so a producer holds sooner than a check would; and a build that starts at 539 s can still outlive the Bash timeout.
risks.mitigation: The design doc states the cap. If Bash kills a running build the slot frees when the wrapper dies. The cap only guarantees the waiting case reaches exit 75.

risks.risk: SIGKILL of the wrapper frees the lock while the child cargo may keep running (workspace denies unsafe, so no exec).
risks.mitigation: Documented trade-off kept from the earlier candidate, in the design doc and the wrapper's module doc; the process-group kill (claude.rs:394) normally kills the child too.

risks.risk: Real-cargo lookup picks the shim itself or finds nothing, which would loop or fail.
risks.mitigation: Lookup skips the shim dir; a test covers it; exit 127 with a clear message when no cargo is found.

risks.risk: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` (allowed to the producer) still compile without a slot.
risks.mitigation: Stated in the design doc and CHANGELOG; gating them is a separate change as the brief limits scope.

risks.risk: A hold at the producer stage discards the producer's work tree, so the next drain starts the producer again.
risks.mitigation: Same as hold_for_disk before the producer; the wording fix (finding 4) and the design doc say so.

risks.risk: CLI tests are timing-sensitive (a forked child can briefly hold a copy of a lock file).
risks.mitigation: Poll `waiting()` and the log, not sleeps, as slots.rs tests do; bounded `take_soon` retry for the last try_acquire; every wait bounded at 10 s with a clear message.

risks.risk: In unit tests athena_bin is /bin/false, so the symlink points to a program that exits 1.
risks.mitigation: The shim lives under the job's own agent/bin dir; a test checks the link target.

risks.risk: The shard-timings line is out of order or flagged by the mirrors check.
risks.mitigation: Run cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards and cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors after the edit; the value is marked as an estimate.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in the new crates/athena-cli/tests/slot_exec.rs. A one-slot SlotQueue is built over a temp dir. `install_cargo_shim` builds the producer env; each child is started with env_clear plus that env. Two processes spawn `<shim>/cargo build`, with a fake cargo later on PATH that appends start and end lines to a log and blocks on a release file. The test waits (polling, bounded 10 s) until `queue.waiting()==1`, asserts the second process has logged no start and `try_acquire` is None, then releases. It asserts the log order first-start, first-end, second-start, and that `try_acquire` succeeds afterwards (bounded retry as `take_soon` in slots.rs).
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: the log shows the second start strictly after the first end, and the slot is acquirable afterwards.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no slot in the wrapper both fake cargos start together and the waiting()==1 and ordering assertions fail. A wrapper that does not release the slot fails the final try_acquire.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the `athena` binary run as `cargo` through the symlink (main.rs argv[0] dispatch into slot_exec::run). Fixtures: temp state dir, install_cargo_shim for the env, a /bin/sh fake cargo that only logs and blocks, and SlotQueue::new over the same dir as observer (exists, slots.rs). slot_exec, the dispatch and install_cargo_shim are added by plan steps 1 to 5.

demonstrations.method: Same test file. One test runs `cargo -q build` and one runs `cargo --locked test` through the shim. The fake cargo logs its args and blocks on a release file. While it is blocked the test asserts `queue.try_acquire()` is None. After release it asserts exit 0, that the args reached the fake unchanged, and that the slot is free again. A third test sets ATHENA_SLOT_HELD to a different dir path in the child's env (the case where a producer's own HELD leaks into a test) and still sees the slot held; a fourth sets it to the wrapper's own slot dir and sees the nested cargo run without a slot and without deadlock on a one-slot queue.
demonstrations.observes: Both gated commands hold the only slot while the fake runs and free it after; args pass through unchanged. The foreign HELD value does not disable the slot, and the matching one does.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lookup that reads only args[0] sees `-q` or `--locked`, takes no slot, and `try_acquire` succeeds while the fake runs. A plain HELD flag would fail the foreign-HELD case.
demonstrations.seam: As criterion 1: one-slot queue so any held slot is visible from outside; fake cargo is a shell script holding no slot logic. All added by steps 1 to 5.

demonstrations.method: Three tests. (a) CLI file: the test holds the only slot with `try_acquire`, installs the shim with a small wait (a `CargoShim` whose build_wait_s is 1, so `producer_slot_wait_s` gives 1), runs `cargo build`, and asserts exit 75, stderr containing 'no build slot free for 1 s; try again', the fake cargo's start marker absent, and `read_wait_note` returning SlotWait{limit_s:1}. (b) env.rs unit test `the_wrapper_wait_is_below_the_bash_timeout`: `producer_slot_wait_s(1800, 600000)` is 540, below 600; `(30, 600000)` is 30; `(1800, 50000)` is 1; and `install_cargo_shim` with the shipped numbers sets ATHENA_SLOT_WAIT_S to 540. (c) run/tests.rs `a_producer_slot_wait_note_holds_the_job_and_does_not_fail_it`: a script for Role::Producer writes the note with `slots::write_wait_note` to `spec.env["ATHENA_SLOT_NOTE"]`; `Athena::go` returns an error that downcasts to SlotWait, state is Dispatched with no outcome or score, `read_slot_hold` is Some, `read_hold` is None, and the 'held       environment: build slot wait' line is printed. A later `retry` lands the job once no note is written.
demonstrations.observes: The wrapper test shows exit 75, the message, an unstarted real cargo and a written note. The env test shows the default wait is below the Bash timeout. The run test shows the job held, not failed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the exit-75 path the wrapper starts cargo or exits 1. Without the cap, (b) fails (1800 not below 600) and the hold is unreachable in real runs. Without the note read in producer_loop, (c) gets a failed or landed job instead of a SlotWait hold.
demonstrations.seam: (a) as criterion 1 with the slot held from outside. (b) `env::producer_slot_wait_s` and `install_cargo_shim`, added by step 2. (c) Production entry point `Athena::go` through producer_loop and produce_and_verify; helpers `athena_with`/`counting` and the FakeAgentDriver script closure that receives the invocation env exist (run/tests.rs, fake.rs). The double only writes the note, which is what the wrapper does in (a); reading and holding the note is production code from steps 4 to 6.

demonstrations.method: CLI test with a one-slot queue whose only slot the test holds throughout. It runs `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo metadata` through the shim with a short wait. For each it asserts the fake cargo ran, exit 0, elapsed time under the wait limit, and no wait note written.
demonstrations.observes: Both commands run to completion at once while every slot is held.
demonstrations.fails_without: If every subcommand took a slot both would block for the wait, exit 75 and never start the fake cargo.
demonstrations.seam: As criterion 1 plus a slot held from outside; added by the same steps.

demonstrations.method: policy.rs unit test `the_shared_global_flag_list_finds_the_subcommand_check_cargo_accepts` loops over CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS. For each flag it asserts `cargo_subcommand([flag, "build"]) == Some("build")` and that `check_cargo` allows `cargo <flag> build`; an unlisted flag gives None and check_cargo refuses it. Existing check_cargo tests run unchanged. Grep for CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS shows one definition and the wrapper reaching it through `policy::cargo_subcommand`.
demonstrations.observes: The new test and every existing policy test pass; the constant changes only in visibility.

demonstrations.method: (b) is the demonstration: a run/tests.rs test records `spec.env` by role over a full job through `Athena::go` with the FakeAgentDriver script closure; the producer env's PATH starts with `<job_dir>/agent/bin` and has the cargo symlink, the reader and verifier envs have PATH equal to the parent's and no ATHENA_SLOT_* keys. (a) An env.rs unit test `the_cargo_shim_goes_first_on_the_producer_path_only` checks install_cargo_shim on a Side::Produce env (shim first, stale link replaced, variables set); it is described as a regression guard, and the Verify/Read half is dropped because `build` is unchanged and cannot fail (finding 5). Inspect `git diff` of env.rs to confirm `build` is unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: The producer PATH starts with the shim dir; reader and verifier PATH values are the parent's.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the shim were installed in `build`, or for every side, the reader and verifier assertions in the run test fail.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go` with the FakeAgentDriver script closure (exists); `install_cargo_shim` and its call in producer.rs are added by steps 2 and 5.
